title: Reconstructing developmental and disease progression with sample-level embeddings
title_zh: 利用样本级嵌入还原发育与疾病进程
abstract: Single-cell genomics is transformative for characterizing cellular heterogeneity, but many biological questions require comparing samples rather than individual cells. Typical analyses compare "case" and "control" groups, ignoring sample-level variation within them. Here, we present scSLIDE (single-cell sample-level inference using density estimation), a framework that transforms each sample's single-cell data into a compact profile describing where its cells are distributed in high-dimensional space. By comparing these density profiles, scSLIDE calculates embeddings to characterize variation across samples. We implement scSLIDE in version 6 of our Seurat package and apply it to COVID-19 infection, Alzheimer's disease, and zebrafish embryogenesis. scSLIDE reveals patient subgroups, reconstructs disease trajectories, and identifies coordinated cellular programs across samples. We discover separable axes of infection and severity, a trajectory of Alzheimer's progression, and embryonic "pseudostages" that vary across and within time points. Our results demonstrate how case-control analyses collapse rich biological variation into binary labels and how sample-level embedding represents a powerful analytical alternative.
abstract_zh: 单细胞基因组学在表征细胞异质性方面具有变革性，但许多生物学问题需要比较样本而非个体细胞。典型的分析将"病例"和"对照"组进行比较，忽略了其内部的样本级变异。本文介绍了scSLIDE（单细胞样本级推断密度估计），该框架将每个样本的单细胞数据转化为一个紧凑的轮廓，描述其细胞在高维空间中的分布位置。通过比较这些密度轮廓，scSLIDE计算嵌入以表征样本间的变异。我们在Seurat包的第6版中实现了scSLIDE，并将其应用于COVID-19感染、阿尔茨海默病和斑马鱼胚胎发育。scSLIDE揭示了患者亚群、重构了疾病轨迹，并跨样本识别协调的细胞程序。我们发现了可分离的感染与严重程度轴、阿尔茨海默病进程轨迹，以及跨时间点和时间点内变化的胚胎"假分期"。我们的结果展示了病例对照分析如何将丰富的生物学变异压缩为二元标签，以及样本级嵌入作为一种强大的分析替代方案。
